independent_computation.step_1_what_bloodsong_actually_does: Per S1 the item has exactly two combat components. (a) Spellblade proc: a DAMAGE component worth 100% base AD as bonus physical damage on the next basic attack within 10s of an ability cast. (b) Expose Weakness: a 4-second DEBUFF on the champion hit, 'causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources'. Component (b) carries no damage term of any kind.
independent_computation.step_2_amp_arithmetic: Expose Weakness is a pure multiplier on damage the target receives: post_amp = post_mitigation_damage * 1.08 (melee holder) or * 1.05 (ranged holder), per S1 + the melee|ranged template ordering fixed by S3. Its own contribution as an independent damage instance is identically 0: raw_expose_weakness = 0 for every target, level, and build. There is no leveling row, no ratio, and no flat term anywhere in the cached entry to price.
independent_computation.step_3_therefore_it_cannot_be_an_event_s: A combat-ledger event needs an entity that produced the packet. Since Expose Weakness produces 0 damage and only rescales packets produced by other entities (S1, S6), 'expose_weakness_Bloodsong' cannot be the source of any damage instance. By S7 the amp folds multiplicatively into the value of the event that actually dealt the damage; it does not split off a separately-sourced event. Whatever damage sat at events[82] was dealt by some roster participant's ability or attack and must be booked to that producer.
independent_computation.step_4_what_the_producer_is: 'E' is a valid producer token: an ability slot (S8). It is the only one of the two candidate values that names an entity capable of dealing damage. So the corrected attribution at this index is the ability slot E.
independent_computation.step_5_scenario_specific_corroboration: The scenario name pins Black Cleaver + Bloodsong on a coupled roster. The single champion-ability interaction with Bloodsong anywhere in the cache is S2: Gangplank E (Powder Keg) - 'Dealing damage with kegs to champions won't apply Expose Weakness to them,' while the same note says 'If the keg destroying attack was empowered with Spellblade, its damage will be added to the explosions' damage' (the sDMG term of the note's formula {aDMG * [2(+0.30)]} + sDMG + cDMG). That is precisely the shape the corrected value asserts: the Spellblade-empowered damage rides the E (keg) event and is booked to E, and the Expose Weakness debuff is NOT applied - and therefore must not appear as a source - on the keg path. Both the general rule (step 3) and this specific carve-out point at 'E'.
independent_computation.step_6_did_the_engine_lose_the_amp: No total is at stake either way: the 8%/5% amp is multiplicative and, by S7, conserved whether it is expressed as a separate row or folded into the producing event. The change is an attribution correction, not a damage change - and the attribution the wiki supports is the producer's, i.e. 'E'.

boundaries_and_residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' lives outside the permitted evidence tree (it is not in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md), so the exact identity of ledger index 82 - which participant, which timestamp - cannot be recovered from cached data alone. The verdict therefore rests on the type-level rule that Expose Weakness can never be a damage source while an ability slot can, plus the Gangplank keg carve-out that independently forbids Expose Weakness on the E path.

If the ledger were a mixed ledger that also records debuff APPLICATION rows, an Expose Weakness row could exist in principle - but per S1 its applier is the empowered BASIC ATTACK ('your next basic attack ... inflict them with Expose Weakness'), never an ability cast, so 'E' would still not be a legitimate source for such a row and the old value would still be wrong on the keg path per S2. Under either reading of the ledger, 'expose_weakness_Bloodsong' is not defensible at this leaf.

'expose_weakness_Bloodsong' does not appear in the sanctioned coarse-source list quoted in S4 (muramana_ability, proc_Eclipse, shaped_charge_Bastionbreaker), so there is no audited exemption keeping it as an intentional catch-all source.
verdict_rationale: Expose Weakness deals zero damage by its own cached wiki text - it is a 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged) multiplier on damage the target takes from all OTHER sources - so it cannot be the source of a combat event; and on the one champion path in the cache where Bloodsong meets an E ability (Gangplank's Powder Keg), the wiki explicitly states kegs never apply Expose Weakness at all while Spellblade damage IS added to the keg explosion. The producer-attributed value 'E' is the correct source; 'expose_weakness_Bloodsong' was a misattribution of an amplifier as a damage producer.
